Four products, one stack: model, edit, publish, ship

Software you can install in one line.

A headless CMS, the console that edits it, a site engine that publishes it, and the CLI that ships all three to a VM you already pay for. Underneath, the .NET libraries they are built on. Open source, MIT or MPL-2.0, already in other people's production.

External dependencies

Arnel Robles, developer from the baryo.

Open to consulting

.NET engineer, 14 years in production software. I build the lean alternatives to the libraries everyone reaches for by default: a mapper without the configuration ceremony, resilience without the abstraction tower, a spreadsheet reader without Interop. Zero external dependencies is the rule, not a feature.

Four products: a headless CMS, its console, a site engine and the Go CLI that deploys them over SSH. Under those, five package families on NuGet and ten utilities on npm. barakocms.com runs on barakoCMS. Open an issue and I am the one who answers it, usually within two working days.

github.com/BaryoDevWritingarnelirobles@gmail.com

Four products, one stack

Model the content, edit it, publish it, ship it to a VM you already have. Each one runs on its own; barakoPress’s compose file runs all four behind Caddy on ports 80 and 443 only.

Live demo, demo_admin
01Modelv4.0 · MPL-2.0

barakoCMS

The headless API

Event-sourced on Marten and Postgres, .NET 10. Multi-tenant, RBAC, MFA, scheduled publishing, thirteen opt-in modules. 2,274 tests against real Postgres and MinIO.

$ curl -O https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BaryoDev/barakoCMS/master/quickstart/docker-compose.yml
$ curl -O https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BaryoDev/barakoCMS/master/quickstart/.env.example
$ cp .env.example .env
$ docker compose up -d
Repo for barakoCMSDocs for barakoCMS
02Editghcr.io · MPL-2.0

barakoBrew

The console

Content types, entries with version history, workflows, roles and health, all against the API. Point the image at any instance, no rebuild. Playwright runs it nightly against the real API.

$ docker run -p 3000:3000 -e NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL=http://localhost:5005 ghcr.io/baryodev/barako-admin:latest
Repo for barakoBrewDemo for barakoBrew
03Publishearly · MIT

barakoPress

The site engine

A blog on barakoCMS, server rendered and cached until the CMS says otherwise. A publish is live in one signed webhook; ordinary traffic never touches Postgres. Feed and sitemap from the same read.

$ git clone https://github.com/BaryoDev/barakoPress && cd barakoPress
$ cp .env.example .env
$ npm install && npm run build && npm start
Repo for barakoPressCaching design for barakoPress
04Shipv0.3.0 · MPL-2.0

BaryoVM

The deploy CLI

PaaS-style releases on VMs you already have, agentless over SSH, in Go. Backs the database up before it touches anything, then verifies the site is serving. Stores key paths, never keys.

$ brew install arnelirobles/tap/baryovm
$ baryovm doctor

Libraries

What the products are built on. 50 packages on NuGet, ten on npm, download counts live from the registries.

Full NuGet profile

Mapsicle

C#

Object mapping, fourteen packages. Benchmarked on x64 and arm64 against AutoMapper and Mapperly, and the numbers say where it loses too.

nuget 2.2.082,489 downloads

barakoCMS

C#

Event-sourced headless CMS on Marten and Postgres. 164 endpoints, 2,274 tests against real Postgres and MinIO. MPL-2.0, every module included.

nuget 4.0.124,186 downloads

Verdict

C#

Result pattern, eight packages. The zero-allocation promise is enforced by benchmark: 0 B measured over 1.6M operations on 8 threads.

nuget 2.8.013,217 downloads

Carom

C#

Retry, timeout, circuit breaker, bulkhead, rate limiting, fallback, hedging. 503 tests on .NET 8 and .NET 10. A leaner Polly.

nuget 2.0.07,835 downloads

Talaan

C#

Spreadsheet and CSV reader, zero dependencies. barakoCMS consumes it as a published package, so the packaging is exercised for real.

nuget 0.1.07,344 downloads

Everything else

NuGet

The two Umbraco packages and an early utility library, published under the same profile.

3 more packages

Merged upstream

Nine merged fixes in libraries I run in production, across three repos totalling 13k stars. Each was found by using the thing, not by browsing for issues, and marten#5215 ships with a reproduction that runs against published NuGet packages so you can watch the bug appear on one version and vanish on the next.

Reproductions
Umbraco CMS5.2k starsInstances sharing a database failed each other's requests registering the same OpenIddict application.2 mergedTestcontainers4.4k starsReplica-set and cluster init were not idempotent, so a reused container stalled against a one-hour timeout.3 mergedMarten3.5k starsHardDeleteWhere could not remove already soft-deleted rows, and returned cleanly either way.4 merged

What I build with

Short list on purpose. Every dependency here had to earn its place.

Languages and backend

C#, TypeScript, Go, SQL
C# for the libraries, TypeScript for the browser work, Go where a single binary matters.
.NET 8 to 10
ASP.NET Core, REST and GraphQL, event sourcing and CQRS-influenced design.
RabbitMQ, SQS, SNS
Messaging, webhooks and background jobs.

Data and cloud

PostgreSQL and Marten
Document storage and event sourcing on one database. Also SQL Server and Redis.
AWS, Azure, Oracle Cloud
CDK, ECS and Fargate; Functions and App Services. Docker everywhere.
BaryoVM
My own agentless deploy CLI. Every BaryoDev deploy goes through it, which is how its gaps get found.

Gates I trust

Testcontainers
Integration tests against real Postgres, MinIO and MongoDB, not mocks.
BenchmarkDotNet
Performance claims are measured and published, including where they lose.
xUnit, Playwright, Vitest
Plus security scanning in CI on every pull request.
